current: ADR 28/01 defines limits on external noise generated by motor vehicles to limit traffic's contribution to community noise, with Annex A measurement methods and instruments. It applies to LE, M and N category vehicles from dates in its table; vehicles complying with ADR 83/00 need not comply. UN R51/01 or 51/02 is deemed equivalent.
proposed: ADR 28/01 limits external vehicle noise for LE, M and N vehicles; vehicles complying with ADR 83/00 need not comply. UN R51/01 or 51/02 is accepted subject to ADR stationary-noise requirements; for goods vehicles and omnibuses it is equivalent only for moving-vehicle tests, with separate stationary-test evidence required.
evidence: Clauses 28.3.1–28.3.2: "provided that the noise level recorded during the test on the vehicle while stationary does not exceed the appropriate limit listed in Table 1"; for goods vehicles and omnibuses equivalence is "relating to tests on vehicles in motion. Additional evidence of compliance with the appropriate stationary test requirements of this Vehicle standard will be required."

current: ADR 58/00 specifies construction requirements for omnibuses designed for, and licensed for, hire and reward, in addition to individual ADRs for omnibuses. It applies to M2 and M3 categories only; UN R52 (01 series) and UN R107 (02-05 series) are deemed equivalent for small omnibuses up to 15 persons.
proposed: ADR 58/00 specifies construction requirements for M2 and M3 omnibuses designed for, and intended for licensing for, hire and reward. For small omnibuses carrying up to 15 persons including the driver, UN R52 (01 series) is an alternative; UN R107 (02–05 series) additionally requires compliance with ADR clauses 58.23 and 58.24.
evidence: Purpose: "omnibuses designed for, and intended for licensing for, hire and reward". Clause 4.2 permits UN R107 for small omnibuses up to 15 persons "provided that the requirements of clauses 58.23 and 58.24 of this standard are met". Clause 4.1 accepts UN R52/01 for the same small-omnibus capacity.

current: ADR 18/03 specifies requirements for the provision of speedometers (and odometer equipment) in vehicles. It applies to LC, LD, LE and all M and N category vehicles from 1 July 2006 (new models) and 1 July 2007 (all models); UN Regulation 39 (00, 01 or 02 series) is deemed equivalent.
proposed: ADR 18/03 specifies requirements for speedometers in LC, LD, LE and all M and N vehicles from 1 July 2006 for new models and 1 July 2007 for all models. UN Regulation 39 in its 00, 01 or 02 series is accepted as an alternative.
evidence: Function and scope: "The function of this vehicle standard is to specify requirements for the provision of speedometers." Appendix A scope and definition 2.1 concern "speedometer equipment including its installation". The word odometer occurs only in the titles of later-series alternative standards; the original-version alternative is also accepted.

Clause 3.1: "applies to the design and construction of LEP, LEG, MA, MB, MC and NA category vehicles". Clause 3.5: "LEP & LEG category vehicles must comply with M1 and N1 category vehicle requirements respectively." Table labels LE as Motor tricycle/L5; L-category vehicle search currently omits them.

Applicability Table C.3 lists "Enclosed vehicles | LEP & LEG | ... | 1 March 1991" and "All vehicles | LEP & LEG | ... | 1 July 1992" under Motor tricycle/L5; also "Light omnibus | MD | M2" and MD1 "up to 3.5 tonnes GVM and up to 12 seats | ... | 1 July 1988". Bus and L-category applicability are absent from the current filters.

Applicability table lists Motor tricycle LE/L5 with LEP "1 July 1992 | Nil" while LEM and LEG are N/A, alongside MA/MB/MC and NA1. This is limited LEP tricycle applicability; the Motorcycle taxonomy bucket is the repository's L-category bucket.

Applicability Table 3.2 lists Motor tricycle LE/L5, "LEP & LEG All vehicles ... 1 July 1992"; Medium goods vehicle NB/N2, NB1 "over 3.5 tonnes up to 4.5 tonnes GVM ... 1 July 1988". Both L-category and N2 vehicles are missing from the current search tags.

current: ADR 11/00 sets requirements for internal sun visors to reduce injury potential to occupants from the visor and adjacent vehicle structure. It requires no sharp rigid mounting edges, energy-absorbing covering and padded mirror edges, and an energy-absorption head-impact test. It applies to passenger cars, light omnibuses and light goods vehicles (and enclosed motor tricycles) from dates in the applicability table.
proposed: ADR 11/00 sets injury-reduction and energy-absorption requirements for internal sun visors and attached mirrors. It applies to M1 passenger vehicles, LEP/LEG motor tricycles, light omnibuses up to 4.5 tonnes GVM, light goods vehicles and NB1 medium goods vehicles up to 4.5 tonnes, from the dates in its applicability table.
evidence: Table 3.2: "LEP & LEG Enclosed vehicles only ... 1 March 1991" then "LEP & LEG All vehicles ... 1 July 1992"; NB1 medium goods vehicles "over 3.5 tonnes up to 4.5 tonnes GVM ... 1 July 1988"; MD1, MD2 and MD3 are applicable, MD4 is Not Applicable. Clauses 11.2–11.3 specify visor mounting, mirror edge covering and energy absorption.
